claims.text: The initial catalyst consists of Pt nanoparticles uniformly dispersed on a γ-Al2O3 support.
An optimized ALD process can deposit a conformal, nanometer-thick, porous CeO2 overlayer on pre-formed Pt/γ-Al2O3.
The deposited CeO2 overlayer encapsulates the Pt nanoparticles.
The CeO2 overlayer acts as a protective barrier against Pt-particle sintering.
The CeO2 overlayer inhibits poisoning of the Pt surface.
Controlled porosity in the CeO2 overlayer maintains access and transport for reactive gas species.
Suppressing agglomeration and poisoning preserves desirable Pt surface electronic properties.
Preserving Pt surface properties maintains high catalytic turnover.
The porous CeO2 overlayer will enhance catalytic activity relative to uncoated Pt/γ-Al2O3.
The porous CeO2 overlayer will enhance catalyst durability relative to uncoated Pt/γ-Al2O3.
The coated catalyst will retain more than 90% of its initial activity after prolonged thermal and chemical aging.
Effective catalytic performance can be maintained with approximately 40% less Pt than in a conventional uncoated Pt/γ-Al2O3 catalyst.
The proposed benefits are expected to persist during thermal cycling from 400°C to 800°C in the presence of sulfur and other exhaust impurities.
A CeO2 overlayer that is too dense or nonporous can compromise reactant access and limit the catalytic benefit.
ALD precursor pulse time and oxidant exposure are critical determinants of overlayer optimization.
Variation in overlayer porosity may change the quantitative activity improvement and achievable reduction in Pt consumption.
